basis: Parametrial infection is a form of pelvic inflammatory disease; its reproductive anatomical site has no axis.
Metastatic tumour directly occupies the brain; the original tumour site is unspecified.
Eversion of the eyelid; eyelids belong to the ocular axis.
Squamous carcinoma arising in the urinary tract, which belongs to the renal axis.
Fungal infection directly ulcerates the cornea.
Premature hormonal activation and sexual maturation constitute an endocrine disorder.
Nonsyndromic inherited sensorineural hearing loss.
Tumour arising in the adrenal medulla; cardiovascular injury is not established as common intrinsic organ damage.
Vascular tumour arising in the retina; associated von Hippel-Lindau manifestations belong to a separate syndrome.
Inherited erythroid, platelet and neutrophil abnormalities, with marrow hypocellularity; all belong to the haematologic axis.
Loss of anterior pituitary hormone secretion defines this endocrine disorder.
Inherited rod-cone retinal degeneration; the metabolic function of IDH3B alone does not establish systemic metabolic disease.
Complex congenital cardiac malformations define the clinically affected phenotype; visceral reversal alone does not establish organ damage.
Autoimmune bilateral granulomatous uveitis; hearing and skin abnormalities are occasional (5-29%) and excluded.
Multiple benign cutaneous sweat-duct tumours.
ETFDH-related metabolic disease usually causes lipid-storage myopathy (>50%); cardiac, hepatic and neurologic injury chiefly affect severe minority forms.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection produces empyema in the pleural space.
Rare oral-acral malformation syndrome indicating oral and limb involvement; no definition or detailed phenotypes supplied to refine classification.
Mitochondrial disorder with cardiomyopathy (4/7); severe myopathy is characteristic, with muscle mtDNA depletion in 5/5; seizures occur in 2/7.
Congenital postaxial extra digits are skeletal malformations.
Lysosomal storage disease causing progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and visual loss affect most patients (>50%) over the course.
Genetically defined Wilms tumour arising in the kidney; radial aplasia is not established as a common feature of this concept.
Skin fragility and nail dystrophy define the disease; oral blistering and enamel hypoplasia are defining gastrointestinal-axis manifestations.
Inherited striate palmoplantar skin thickening; keratoderma reported in 14/14 patients.
Smooth-muscle malignancy arising in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; smooth muscle alone does not qualify as musculoskeletal.
